message.content:
In Texas, tenants have several statutory protections and responsibilities under the Texas Property Code and related laws. Here’s an overview of your key rights: | Category | What You’re Entitled To | |----------|------------------------| | **Security Deposit** | • Landlords may charge up to one month’s rent (or two if the lease is for a furnished unit).
• Must be returned within 30 days after you move out, minus any lawful deductions. | | **Habitability** | • Landlord must keep the premises safe, sanitary, and in good repair.
• Must maintain plumbing, heating, electrical, and structural integrity. | | **Right to Quiet Enjoyment** | • Landlord cannot enter without proper notice (usually 24‑hour written notice for non‑emergency reasons). | | **Notice Requirements** | • For non‑payment of rent: 3‑day notice to pay or vacate.
• For lease termination: 30‑day notice for month‑to‑month agreements; 60‑day for longer leases. | | **Discrimination Protections** | • Landlords cannot discriminate based on race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, familial status, or other protected classes. | | **Repair & Deduct / Rent‑With‑hold** | • If landlord fails to fix major problems, you may repair and deduct from rent or withhold rent until repairs are made (subject to strict conditions). | | **Eviction Process** | • Must follow court procedures; no “self‑eviction” or “no‑court” eviction. | | **Lease Terms** | • Lease must be in writing if it lasts longer than one year.
• Must include rent amount, due date, security deposit, and lease duration. | | **Landlord Access** | • Landlord may enter for inspections, repairs, or showings with reasonable notice (except emergencies). | | **Tenant Insurance** | • While not required by law, it’s wise to carry renters insurance for liability and personal property protection. | ### Practical Tips 1. **Document Everything** – Keep copies of all communications, receipts, and photos of any damage or maintenance issues. 2. **Know Your Lease** – Read it thoroughly; it may contain additional obligations or rights beyond the statutory minimums. 3. **Use Written Notices** – Send notices via certified mail or email with read receipts to create a paper trail. 4. **Seek Legal Aid** – If you face eviction or disputes, consider contacting a local tenant advocacy group or legal aid organization. If you need help drafting a lease or a notice, let me know and I can generate a template for you.
